Dr Jack Thomas
Gastroenterologist
Department of Gastroenterology
City Hospital
Main Road
Stillwater

21/02/2015

Dear Dr Thomas,

Re: Mr. Patrick Newtown                           DOB 06/07/1989

I am writing to refer Mr. Newtown, a 25-year-old accountant, whose symptoms and signs are suggestive of
inflammatory bowel disease. Your assessment would be highly appreciated.

Mr. Newtown is single. Unfortunately, he is a smoker. Moreover, he has suffered from bilateral mild
intermittent wrist pain during the previous 6 months. Regarding his family history, his uncle has been
suffering from Crohn’s disease.

Today, Mr. Newtown presented with a 4-month history of mild diarrhea, mild lower quadrant abdominal
pain, lethargy and a loss of appetite. Additionally, he lost 3 kg from his weight. Apart from diffuse       Commented [AH1]: has lost 3kg
abdominal tenderness, his examination was unremarkable. Consequently, some laboratory tests were
requested. The test results showed an increase in WCC, CRP and ESR levels, but RCC and Hb concentration
were low. Furthermore, the ordered faecal occult blood test was positive. Therefore, I suspected
inflammatory bowel disease, for which the patient was advised to quit smoking and consult a
gastroenterologist.

In light of the above, the patient is being referred for further management. Should you have any queries,
please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Doctor

                              simple and complex sentences. Some
                              weak/unnecessary wording is evident.
 Estimated Grade               B+
 Advice                       1. Revise vocabulary to ensure a strong,
                                  professional tone.
                              2. Always proofread the letter after finishing
                                  writing it.
